title: Concession in an Essay: jóllehet, noha, ámbár, holott

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: You know *jóllehet*, *mindazonáltal* and *holott* from B2 Unit 16, and *bár* and *noha* from earlier units. In an essay they weigh conflicting evidence more precisely than plain *de*. This lesson adds the choice between them. *Jóllehet*, *noha* and *ámbár* introduce a subordinate clause acknowledging a valid counter-point before the main thesis is affirmed: *Jóllehet a gazdasági mutatók javulnak, a társadalmi feszültségek nem enyhülnek.*

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: Look at *holott*: unlike neutral *noha*, *holott* carries an adversative, almost indignant overtone, highlighting a stark contradiction between reality and expectation: *Mindenki elvárta a segítséget, holott senki sem tett érte semmit.*

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: Although the theory is appealing... (measured concession)
Even though he arrived late... (formal concession)
Albeit I acknowledge his merits... (elevated concession)
He didn't help, whereas he easily could have. (sharp contrast)
